label: copy phase: input v/w/e/s while outputting s/j/c/v/z/w/f/e
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original or delimiter steps), from recall_idx 2 onward, with peak rate at recall_idx 2 (the step right after the first copied input, 30% of mass). Activation is driven mainly by the input token: v (39% of mass, 11.6x lift), w (26%), e (14%), s (11%); together these cover about 90% of mass but only ~4% of such steps fire. The output token (s, j, c, v, z, w, f, e lifted 4-8x) and, more weakly, the previous token (e, w, c, v, z, s, b, t, f) raise the firing rate, so the unit acts like a conjunctive token-identity code and not a clean concept. Rate goes down as the number of digits in the sequence goes up. Strongest activations are in short L=3-4 sequences at step L+2, e.g. f w c <DEL> f [w], e v k <DEL> e [v]. Adding the prev_tok condition raises precision to about 0.25 but halves recall. It does not fire on first occurrences of tokens or on digit inputs.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=11: v, w, e, s; t=12: v, w, s, e; t=10: v, w, e, s) and the token being output (most: s, j, c, v, z, w; least: y, x, g, 0); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=4 & t=6, recall_idx=3.
